messages:
emma_support: Customer (acme-inc) reported a ~45s window of 429s even though their dashboard shows ~120 burst credits available. They sent a few example request headers and a short timeline. Can SRE take a look?

liam_sre: On it. Do we have the raw response headers from the failing requests? need X-Burst-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset and any X-Scale hints. Also what model/route?

emma_support: Sent headers snippet from customer: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 2000`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-Burst-Credits: 120`, `X-Burst-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 24`. Route: /v1/generate (gpt-medium), short prompt but high concurrency (many parallel calls).

nina_engineer: Quick thought — burst credits are one axis but smoothing window and fractional refill matter. If they hit a very short, high concurrency spike we can drain bucket faster than refill. What was the concurrency pattern?

carlos_support: Customer said spike was ~150 simultaneous requests for ~30s when they booted a batch job. Not sustained. They expected burst cushion to cover it.

liam_sre: That pattern matches a token-bucket drain. Smoothing policy can limit how fast credits are consumed by spreading allowance across a window. If window is small or disabled, parallel bursts can exhaust remaining credits immediately.

olivia_pm: Is there a safe, short-term mitigation we can tell them while we investigate? They’re on hosted Standard plan.

nina_engineer: Two quick options to offer: 1) Client-side: jittered exponential backoff + queueing/concurrency cap (e.g., cap to 20 concurrent). 2) Server-side: enable a longer smoothing window or fractional refill for that customer (if allowed by plan) to spread replenishment across seconds.

liam_sre: I'll check logs and rate-limit metrics. Running a quick query for the customer’s token-bucket traces now: `svc.ratelimit.tokens.consume{customer:acme-inc} | topk(50) by time`

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of rate-limit smoothing tweak rolled at 2026-03-15T11:58:02Z to 3 regions (no rollback).

liam_sre: Confirmed — we received 150 simultaneous consume spikes, bucket went from 120 -> 0 in ~6s. Refill rate = ~2 credits/s (default). Smoothing was set to minimal for this tenant (legacy config). So expected behavior.

emma_support: Customer asking why dashboard shows 120 credits but they still got 429s — can we summarize simply?

nina_engineer: TL;DR: Dashboard shows total credits available, but burst consumption is per-second limited by smoothing/refill. If many parallel requests consume at once, the visible credits can be depleted faster than they refill; the dashboard number is not a guarantee you can burn that many credits instantly.

carlos_support: I'll message them: recommend immediate client-side concurrency cap + retry-backoff, and offer to enable longer smoothing window for 24h to see if it helps. Want me to open a config change ticket?

olivia_pm: Yes please open ticket and include suggested guardrails and risk note (longer smoothing slightly increases tail latency for short bursts). Also doc update: clarify "burst credits" UI to mention smoothing/refill interplay.

liam_sre: Created ticket INF-4821 to flip smoothing to 10s window + fractional refill for acme-inc for 24h. Added logs + timeline. Putting a tentative rollout at 15:30 UTC after approval.

emma_support: Thanks — I’ll reply to customer with the action plan and immediate client-side mitigations.

nina_engineer: For engineering follow-up: consider exposing a per-tenant instantaneous-consumption metric in Console (e.g., peak-1s consumption) and a small UI hint about refill rate. Makes these conversations easier.

carlos_support: Customer accepted the 24h trial and will monitor. They also sent a repro script — I attached it to the ticket.

liam_sre: Marking thread resolved for now; will update when rollout completes. :white_check_mark:
